children: Consolidated revenue rises 33 per cent to Rs 5,960 crore in the September quarter as the company proposes a 51 per cent stake in the entity holding rights to Chhattisgarh’s Phutamura coal block

Shyam Metalics and Energy reported an 88.4 per cent year-on-year increase in consolidated net profit attributable to owners of the parent company at Rs 493.35 crore for the quarter ended 30 September 2026, compared with Rs 261.76 crore in the corresponding quarter last year.

Consolidated revenue from operations increased 33.4 per cent to Rs 5,960.19 crore during the second quarter of FY27, against Rs 4,467.40 crore a year earlier. Total income rose to Rs 5,994.34 crore from Rs 4,536.53 crore, according to the company's unaudited financial results approved by the board on 31 October.

Consolidated profit after tax stood at Rs 510.99 crore, of which Rs 493.35 crore was attributable to owners of the parent company and Rs 17.64 crore to non-controlling interests. Earnings per share increased to Rs 18.36 from Rs 9.36 in the year-ago quarter. For the six months ended 30 September 2026, consolidated revenue from operations stood at Rs 11,415.28 crore, compared with Rs 8,890.39 crore in the corresponding period last year.

Alongside the quarterly results, the board approved a proposal to acquire a 51 per cent controlling equity stake in Alom Solar, the entity that holds the mining rights for the Phutamura coal block in Raigarh district, Chhattisgarh.

The coal block covers approximately 7.324 sq km and has estimated reserves of around 170 million tonnes. Shyam Metalics said the proposed acquisition would support strategic backward integration by securing long-term coal supplies for captive power generation and its steel manufacturing operations.

The transaction is subject to execution of definitive agreements and necessary statutory approvals. Alom Solar will become a subsidiary of Shyam Metalics upon completion of the acquisition. The company has indicated a completion timeline of on or before 30 November 2026.

The board has also proposed an initial capital expenditure of approximately Rs 360 crore for the development and operationalisation of the Phutamura coal block. Shyam Metalics' proposed 51 per cent contribution to the initial capital expenditure is approximately Rs 183.60 crore, while the remaining 49 per cent will be funded by its joint venture partner.
